findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A)  Inspectors observed multiple food items including but not limited to chicken, beans, and pork in stainless steel food containers stored in the walk-in cooler and the stainless steel double doors standing cooler in the kitchen. Inspectors also saw a container of chicken that was dated12/25/25 but the used by date had expired. PIC told inspectors that the food items were made the day before. PIC discarded the container of chicken dated 12/25/25 as a corrective action. PIC also instructed a staff member to properly date the food items that were not properly dated marked. Ensure that food items that are prepared and being stored for more than 24-hours are properly date marked and stored. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple employee drinks uncovered sitting on the table next to the hard shell fried ice cream waffles in the kitchen. Staff were educated to only have closed beverages and to handle them in a way that prevents contamination. Ensure that personal drinks in that kitchen are covered with a lid and have straw inserted and stored in a way that prevents contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee was washing their while hands wearing gloves. The employee was informed that gloves are single-use and cannot be washed. They removed their gloves and went to grab new gloves. The inspector informed the employee that they must wash their hands before donning gloves. While hand washing, the employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. The inspector educated the PIC that a barrier must be used to turn off the faucet. The inspector proceeded to demonstrate the proper hand washing procedure for the employees in the kitchen and the PIC translated. Ensure that all employees always used the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed there were two coolers for cold holding foods at 14F or below during the inspection:

(1) The standing refrigerator was observed to malfunction distorting the temperature of various food items stored it. The following food items were discarded due to the refrigerator malfunction.
1. Cheese dips (9 containers) = 49-51F
2. Salsa = 49F
3. carnitas = 52F
4. Tamale =49.2F
5. Sheers cake (2 Containers)= 51F
6. Stuffed peppers = 48.7F
Discussed with PIC that the above items were to be discarded because they had been prepared 3/07/25 and place in the refrigerator from the preparation date. Four containers of beans were observed to have internal temperatures between 39-42F and were immediately moved into a functioning cooler. Ensure that equipments are routinely checked for temperature observation to avoid food spoilage.

(2) The prep cooler at the bar was not cold holding foods above 41F. The following temperatures were reordered:
1. Diced tomatoes 51F
2. Sour scream 55F
3. Guac 55F
The temperature-control for safety (TCS) foods inside the cooler (diced tomatoes, pico, sour cream, cheese, and ranch) were discarded during the inspection. The mango hot sauce was non-TCS and allowed to remain inside the cooler. The PIC will be using ice baths to keep TCS items inside the cooler below 41F or under. The PIC was instructed to check the temperature regularly to ensure that the ice baths are sufficient for cold holding. The PIC will be using ice baths until the cooler is cold holding all foods at 41F or below.

 The PIC called and scheduled maintenance for tomorrow. The inspector will follow-up to check on the temperatures for both coolers on 3/14/2025. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: An employee was observed to wash their hands for less than 20 seconds and also not use a barrier to shut off the water. This behavior was corrected on site and PIC was able to translate the proper procedure to wash hands to the entire kitchen staff. The employee was observed to correctly wash their hands after being educated. Esquire all employees are properly trained on how and when to proeprly wash their hands. 
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: An employee was observed to handle their phone and then resume food preparation activities. This behavior was corrected on site and the employee was instructed to wash their hands before continuing their food prep activities. PIC was able to educate this employee and the entire staff on the importance of hand washing and when to wash hands after contamination.  
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The hand washing sink in the kitchen was ob served to be obstructed with a pan soaking in the basin of the sink. The bar hand sink was observed to be blocked with a glass cleaner and a mop handle. These items were removed from their locations and PIC educated staff on the importance of maintaining the hand sinks to be accessible at all times and can only be used for hand washing. Ensure hand sinks are maintained accessible and only used for hand washing. This is a repeat violation from the 2/20/24 original inspection and the facility will receive a Warning Notice to document the violation. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: There was observed a pan of chicken int he double door cooler in the kitchen with a date of 6/25. This item was pulled from service and discarded during today’s inspection due to being past the 7 day rule. Ensure that all food items are checked and either used or discarded on the 7th day after prep. 
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: There is observed a missing piece of plastic on the bottom of the standing freezer in the prep room which has exposed the insulation of the unit. Ensure repairs are made to this unit to maintain the equipment in good repair. 
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The fan being used in the prep room is observed to be coated in dust/soils. Ensure this fan is cleaned to remove the current buildup of dust/soils and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Not all employees have a valid food handler’s certificate. Ensure that all employees earn a Food Handler’s certificate within 30 days of hire.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
